speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a child experiencing frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mouth or eyes, and tiny red spots on your skin. To understand what is causing this, have these bleeding episodes started suddenly, and do they happen with minor bumps or without any injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The clinical presentation of mucosal bleeding and petechiae in a young child is most consistent with isolated thrombocytopenia. I request a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count to confirm the diagnosis.
